entry.title: Panda Bear Remixes Grace Ives’ “Stupid Bitches”
entry.summary: Noah Lennox gives Girlfriend’s standout closer a near-total overhaul
entry.content:
Panda Bear’s Noah Lennox has put his spin on Grace Ives’ “Stupid Bitches,” the standout closer of her new album Girlfriend. Lennox’s version is a near-total overhaul; he cut all new vocals and gave the song’s instrumental a dubby rework. “I'm a huge Panda Bear fan, I am so so happy he did this,” Ives said in press materials. “My new favorite song.” Listen below.

Ives shared Girlfriend, her follow-up to 2022’s Janky Star, in April. Come spring she’ll lend support to Olivia Rodrigo on the European leg of the pop star’s Unraveled Tour.

This year saw Lennox reunite with Sonic Boom’s Pete Kember for A ? of When, their second joint album. He’s also got a live album, PB Band Live 25 at Power Station, on the way next month.

Find out why I named “Stupid Bitches” one of 26 Songs I Want to Hear in the Girls Reboot.

entry.title: Shygirl, Brutalismus 3000, Nirosta Steel Feature on Club Kid Companion EP
entry.summary: Out now, the record includes two covers of Arthur Russell’s “Boy With a Smile”
entry.content:
The soundtrack to Jordan Firstman’s buzzy A24 debut, Club Kid is here. The appropriately club-centric focused EP features Nirosta Steel and Christine and the Queens, who both offer their own takes on avant-garde composer Arthur Russell’s “Boy With a Smile.” Other contributors include Moby, Brutalismus 3000, and Shygirl, who appears as herself in the film. Listen to the songs below.

The A24 feature Club Kid follows a Brooklyn club promoter (Firstman) who lives a hedonistic life until he experiences a rude awakening when he realizes he has a son. The film also stars Cara Delevingne, Miss Benny, Saturn Risin9 as well as involves New York’s nightlife scene, including Amanda Lepeore, Shawn Dickerson, and River Moon.

Read Walden Green’s new review of Shygirl’s Swallow!.

entry.title: Hayley Williams Brings Out Seu Jorge to Cover David Bowie
entry.summary: The Paramore singer and Life Aquatic star also duetted on “Zissou” in São Paulo
entry.content:
Hayley Williams surprised fans in São Paulo last night by inviting samba legend and all-around Brazilian great Seu Jorge to the stage for a pair of duets. Jorge started with an acoustic, Williams-assisted rendition of his cover of David Bowie’s “Life on Mars?” After that, he backed Williams on her thematically twinned track “Zissou.” Watch clips below.

The latter song, taken from Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party, features a verse in Portuguese that was inspired by Jorge’s musical turns in Wes Anderson’s The Life Aquatic With Steve Zissou OST—including “Life on Mars?”—as Williams told Billboard Brasil in an interview. She recently shared a video for another track from the LP, “Dream Girl in Shibuya.” Jorge continues to release albums of original music, the latest being May’s The Other Side.

entry.title: Drake Updates Take Care With New Song “Hate Sleeping Alone”
entry.summary: Get your brood on with an unearthed cut from the 2011 album
entry.content:
To celebrate the 15th anniversary of his 2011 album Take Care, Drake has dug back in the archives and unearthed a new song from the original sessions, “Hate Sleeping Alone.” Grab a golden chalice, light a candle, and give it a listen below.

Longtime Drake devotees are likely familiar with “Hate Sleeping Alone”—the track has long floated around online via exclusive digital editions, and has been available on Apple Music. The difference is that now, you can listen to it on YouTube and across most other streaming platforms (except Spotify, for reasons unclear).

After a long period of inactivity post-Kendrick beef, Drake dropped a metric ton of music this year. He released three albums in one day in May—Iceman, Habibti, and Maid of Honour—all of which came with accompanying visuals collected as the short film FOMO. Drizzy has also kept busy since, remixing Ella Langley’s monster hit “Choosin’ Texas” with Don Toliver, and linking up with Future, Loe Shimmy, and Travis Scott on last week’s “Ya Hit.”

entry.title: 9 New Albums You Should Listen to Now: 2hollis, Armand Hammer, and More
entry.summary: Stream new releases from 2hollis, Ecco2k, Armand Hammer, and U2
entry.content:
With so much good music being released all the time, it can be hard to determine what to listen to first. Every week, Pitchfork offers a run-down of significant new releases available on streaming services. This week’s batch includes new albums from 2hollis, Ecco2k, Armand Hammer, and U2. Subscribe to Pitchfork’s New Music Friday newsletter to get our recommendations in your inbox every week. (All releases featured here are independently selected by our editors. When you buy something through our affiliate links, however, Pitchfork earns an affiliate commission.)

2hollis: Pirouette [Interscope]

Underground-to-mainstream export 2hollis has successfully translated the ragged energy of post-rage into a bona fide pop career. Pirouette meets his skyrocketing profile head-on, going bigger in every possible department. It’s longer, the files are more complicated, the lore is headier, and the sonic profile itself is vast: Emo, pop rock, twee revival, ambient, and choral music all slot into a larger umbrella of pop-EDM. Tying it all together is charismatic Hollis, who matures on sultry, tactile tracks like “Skin” (“Only once I’m under your skin will I feel close enough to you”) and “Sex” (need I elaborate?). Though the album is largely self-produced, Mk.gee notches a writing and production credit on “Human After All.”

Listen on Apple Music
Listen on Spotify

Buy at Rough Trade

Armand Hammer: Snakes and Ladders [Backwoodz]

Armand Hammer, the duo of Elucid and Backwoodz founder billy woods, make their music sound like it is being recited just a foot away from you. That quality is omnipresent on Mercy follow-up Snakes and Ladders. Suffused with political, economic, and technological dread, the album overflows with intimate yarns and moreish imperfections—pianos with no keys, swamps, amd county calls, but also effervescent laughter and Tropical Punch. The production plants you right in the center of it all, within miniature universes where cars rush by, blunted minor chords slink, and haunted melodies loop and reverse.

Ecco2k: Echo [9th]

Despite being an essential Drain Gang member since the 2010s, Ecco2k had only released one solo album, 2019’s E, until now. Carefully crafted over six years, Echo takes the Swedish musician’s world-building to astonishing heights, refining the cloud rap he helped pioneer while escaping its nebulous borders. “Industrial Synth”’s slashes of electric guitar evoke the perkiness of pop rock, “Swimming in Fountains” teems with gurgling, cybernetic IDM synths, and the gliding trip-hop of “Cuban Heel” sounds like an Erika de Casier deep cut. The lyrics tell of molten hot interiors, arrows through the heart, and loveless animals. Echo makes the case for letting the music brew on that hard drive a bit longer. Read more in Kieran Press-Reynolds’ new profile Ecco2k’s Long, Long Coming of Age.

Krill: Secret Language [Exploding in Sound]

Before Krill established their weirdo spin on indie rock in Boston in the early 2010s, the trio grew up in the greater Chicago area before relocating for college. Three albums, one breakup, and a handful of moves later, Krill are back to drumming up new music in the comfort of their hometown. Secret Language, their first full-length in 11 years, takes all the tangled thoughts and pensive observations that are Krill’s bread and butter, and fits them to new musings about parenthood, hobbies, and responsibilities in the modern world. It’s heavy stuff if you let it be, but as always, Krill extend an inviting hand to show you around.

U2: Carnaval de Luz [Island]

A decade has passed since we last got an album of originals from U2, and they’ve clearly had time on their minds. The impetus for Carnaval de Luz arose after drummer Larry Mullen Jr. injured his neck, bringing into focus the four-person rock ecosystem the band has sustained since the late 1970s. After sessions with Brian Eno and Jacknife Lee materialized into the EPs Days of Ash and Easter Lily, Carnaval De Luz closed the loop on their creative return. It comes complete with a duet featuring the final verse Dolly Parton ever recorded.

Fucked Up: Year of the Rooster [Tankcrimes]

Fucked Up’s second album of the year—well, third, depending on your semantic approach to double albums—doubles as the continuation of their Zodiac Cycle and triples as the final installment of their Grass Can Move Stones trilogy. Fans of franchises, concept albums, neoclassical storytelling, and epic hardcore riven with tangents and tributaries will find plenty to tangle with here. Damien Abraham and his veteran accomplices, including Zodiac series regular Tuka Mohammed, ride into a battle of the earworms with guests including Thurston Moore, Black Flag’s Keith Morris, and the Dolly Mixture’s Debsey Wykes.

Snoh Aalegra: Legendary Love [Stem]

The romance that gives Snoh Aalegra’s new album its title is more than just legend. The Iranian Swedish singer tracked the LP over the course of a two-and-a-half year partnership that she says “brought me back to the era of music I fell in love with growing up.” That means warm, silky production inspired by 1980s and ’90s R&B, with assists from Nile Rodgers and Raphael Saadiq. Legendary, indeed.

Aesop Rock and Blockhead: Trouble Mountain [Rhymesayers]

When the rapper Aesop Rock and producer Blockhead were growing up, you couldn’t turn on a TV in the tristate area without being inundated with commercials for pristine ski trips to the Poconos. Neither skied nor had equipment, but the promise of a proper ski lodge party always rang as both enticing and empty: like, “must be nice.” Trouble Mountain, the duo’s first joint album since 2021, takes that fantasy and runs away with it, reimagining the Poconos retreat they saw on primetime as a place where, as Aesop says, “You might meet your future spouse or you might have to fight some local ski gangs.” ’Tis the season!

All roads lead to Indiana University for the trio of Anna Butterss, Ben Lumsdaine, and John Raymond. Butterss is a chameleonic stylist who plays as nicely off their jazz contemporaries (and SML bandmates) as alternative rockers like Phoebe Bridgers and Neko Case. More than a decade after their campus improvisation series Call and Response, the trio revived its interweaving chemistries for this studio session, as spontaneous as it is grounded.

entry.title: Zsela Invites You to The Party With New Album
entry.summary: Listen to “Real Romantic” from the Los Angeles singer’s new LP for Nice Life
entry.content:
Zsela is getting ready for The Party—that is, her full-length follow-up to 2024’s Big for You and debut for new label Nice Life. The Brooklyn-born, Los Angeles-based singer released lead track “Kinda Guy” last month, and today’s announcement comes with a sultry second single, “Real Romantic.” Listen to that below ahead of the album release on February 19, 2027.

Zsela co-wrote and produced the song with Zack Sekoff and Daniel Memmi; Sekoff worked across the album with Zsela, and the duo brought in contributors including Dijon, Daniel Aged, and Nick Weiss. Zsela will launch the album with a show at L.A.’s 2220 Arts + Archives next week, on November 19.

entry.title: Hear U2’s Posthumous Dolly Parton Duet
entry.summary: “Torn” is the closing track off the band’s new album, Carnaval de Luz
entry.content:
U2 have released their new album Carnaval de Luz, and with it their duet with the late Dolly Parton. The LP’s closing track, “Torn” is supposedly the last song Parton recorded before her death in August. It was co-written with Snow Patrol’s Johnny McDaid, and features steadfast U2 collaborator Daniel Lanois on pedal steel. “Torn apart these loving hearts that beat and break the same,” Parton and Bono sing atop a gentle synth pulse and spare, echoing drums. “We share a house divided and the blood that fills our veins.” Listen below.

Carnaval de Luz marks U2’s first studio album since 2017’s Songs of Experience. It was preceded this year by two surprise EPs—Days of Ash and Easter Lily. “Torn” may be Dolly Parton’s final song, but it won’t be the last Dolly Parton song we ever hear. There apparently exists an unheard recording, titled “My Place in History,” sealed away in a vault at Dollywood, to be unsealed on Parton’s 100th birthday in 2046.

Read Sam Sodomsky’s new review of Carnaval de Luz.

entry.title: Watch Rosalía Perform a Lux Medley at the 2026 Latin Grammys
entry.summary: Her 2025 album is up for seven statuettes tonight
entry.content:
Rosalía opened up the Latin Grammys tonight, offering a medley of songs from her 2025 album Lux. The record picked up seven nominations tonight, and the Catalan singer rose to the occasion wearing a golden gown and surrounded by rows of dancers to perform “La Rumba Del Perdón,” “La Perla,” and “Dios Es Un Stalker.” Watch it below.

It’s already been an exciting month for Rosalía. This week, her role in Wet—a so-far-extremely-mysterious new film from Alma Har’el—was confirmed. Shooting on that is not yet under way. And on November 7, she celebrated Lux’s one-year anniversary by sharing a playlist of songs that inspired the record, including selections from Kate Bush, Yung Lean, Mozart, Caetano Veloso, and more. So far tonight, Rosalía has nabbed one win, for Best Pop Song for “La Perla.”

entry.title: Saba and Pivot Gang Set 2027 North American Tour
entry.summary: The All My Friends Tour is the Chicago rap collective’s first proper run since 2019
entry.content:
Saba and Pivot Gang are bringing all my friends on the road with them next year—no, seriously! The All My Friends Tour, the Chicago rap collective’s first proper run since 2019, kicks off on March 5 in Atlanta, and will feature all five crew members: Saba, MFnMelo, Joseph Chilliams, Frsh Waters, and daedaePIVOT. The run closes out on March 24 with an all-ages show in Los Angeles. Check out all the dates below.

The tour announcement lands just a few weeks after Pivot Gang shared their first new music in two years, “Location."They released their last posse tape, You Can’t Sit With Us, in 2019—it was their final project with former in-house producer Squeak, who died in 2021. Although Pivot Gang as a collective have remained relatively quiet since then, Saba has continued to drop steadily. Last year alone, he shared a solo EP, Coffee!, and a collaborative album with No ID, From the Private Collection of Saba and No ID.

Before they embark on the tour, Pivot Gang will play a hometown show at Thalia Hall on December 19 in honor of John Walt Day. The annual benefit concert is held in memory of Pivot Gang rapper Walter “John Walt” Long Jr., who was murdered in 2017.

entry.title: Ralphie Choo Returns With New Album and Song
entry.summary: “El Hueso” leads Charmain “Le Grand Architecte” ahead of its February release
entry.content:
Ralphie Choo is gearing up to release his first new album in nearly four years. Charmain “Le Grand Architecte” is out February 26 via Rusia-IDK/Warner, and it follows the Madrid artist’s 2023 record, Supernova. Leading the new LP is the single “El Hueso,” which you can listen to below.

When describing the backstory of “El Hueso,” he said: “It’s all about the thrill – the thrill of being in the thick of things with your people, of hanging out with them, singing, dancing, and showing off with them. To have been through the rough times and now be able to enjoy the good times – and even ride out the rough times again. It’s about setting the trend without even trying, about bringing out the best in the outsiders we welcome.”

Charmain “Le Grand Architecte” also includes the song “Amarillo Nena,” which came out last month. In the years between Supernova and now, Ralphie Choo has been trying to explore new ground in music, building off the eccentric genre-skipping work of his past. At the start of the year, he dropped “Rocco” and “Tentacíon,” but it’s unclear if those will be included on the LP, or if fans can expected a reprise of his collaborative efforts with Rosalía.

Read about “Máquina Culona” in The 100 Best Songs of 2023.

entry.title: Phoebe Bridgers Extends Tour Into 2027
entry.summary: Lucky residents of Portland and Spokane can see Grouper open for the singer-songwriter
entry.content:
Grab your Yondr pouch: Phoebe Bridgers is continuing her Lost Tour into 2027. The North American arena run now extends through mid-May, and what’s more, will bring about the first-ever Grouper arena shows. You read that right—Liz Harris will open for Bridgers in Portland, Oregon and Spokane, Washington. Paper Wings and Christian Lee Hutson will then handle support for the rest of the dates. Find the full list of Bridgers’ 2027 performances below, including her fest spots at Coachella, Primavera, and St. Charles, Iowa’s Hinterland Festival.

Bridgers shared Lost Weekend, her first solo album in six years, back in August; last month, she dropped a Tidal-exclusive live EP of songs from the LP, recorded at Madison Square Garden. This year has also seen Bridgers discover a passion for acting—she’s lent her voice to short films from My Chemical Romance and Conor Oberst, and played a substantial part in Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime, for which she also wrote an original song. She’ll be the musical guest on Saturday Night Live this weekend, opposite seven-time host John Mulaney.

entry.title: The Weeknd Broods, Sings Karaoke in “Hong Kong” Video
entry.summary: The power ballad features Cantopop singer Faye Wong
entry.content:
The Weeknd has shared his first single of the year. Debuted live in the titular metropolis last month, “Hong Kong” is a duetted power ballad with Cantopop singer Faye Wong. The video, starring the model Ming Xi, intercuts slick footage of crystalline cars and big city lights with scenes of Abel Tesfaye brooding, pining, and belting karaoke on a set that may or may not be anywhere near Hong Kong. Watch it go down below.

The song’s live premiere took place at Kai Tak Stadium on October 24, where the video played on a giant screen. The single dropped in China a week later; a full streaming release on Western services has not yet been announced. Since releasing Hurry Up Tomorrow, the Weeknd has also debuted the Anitta-assisted “Rio” and a song that samples the theme from Neon Genesis Evangelion.

entry.title: Jeanne River Recruits Cameron Winter for Debut Single
entry.summary: “PP2” introduces the Brooklyn singer and electroacoustic composer, with prepared piano from the Geese frontman
entry.content:
Jeanne River, the leftfield folk project of Brooklynite Jeanne Hill, has debuted with a Cameron Winter-assisted single called “PP2.” The Geese prodigy plays prepared piano on the bric-a-brac tune; Hill contributes vocals, ukulele, celesta, production, and other technical duties that make use, in part, of an Ampex MM1200 reel-to-reel tape machine. Hill also made the cover art with photographer Liselotte Davis, which you can find below, along with the video.

Budding Jeanne River fans can catch her tomorrow (November 12) at Night Club 101 in Manhattan, on a bill with Caroline’s Jasper Llewellyn. A Philadelphia show supporting Joanne Robertson is lined up for April 8, 2027.

entry.title: Beyoncé Recreates Sade’s Love Deluxe Album Cover
entry.summary: She also paid homage to Diana Ross in a new i-D feature
entry.content:
Beyoncé might not say much of anything outside her music but she’ll never pass on an opportunity to gush about Sade, from shouting her out in a Harper’s Bazaar interview to posting a handwritten letter on her website about what the singer means to her. “For years, I've turned to Sade for inspiration,” she wrote in 2012. “I cannot even begin to count the nights, days, hard times—when I need her—she is there, to inspire me, and brighten me. Her music has been a true friend, as all true music should be.”

Bey’s latest Sade tribute? Recreating the 1992 Love Deluxe cover, in a new photo shoot and (likely emailed) interview in i-D Magazine. Alas, the Beyoncé Q&A doesn’t mention Sade herself—it’s largely about the hair product line Cécred—but it does include another homage, to Diana Ross’ Forever boxset art. You can check that one out over on i-D. Sade is set to be inducted into—but not appear at—the Rock Hall on November 14.

entry.title: Phoebe Bridgers, Slayyyter, Billy Strings to Headline Hinterland 2027
entry.summary: The three-day music festival returns to St. Charles, Iowa next summer
entry.content:
Hinterland Music Festival is headed back to Iowa next summer for another long weekend of middle-American field frolicking. Pitchfork can exclusively reveal the 2027 lineup, which features headliners Phoebe Bridgers, Slayyyter, and Billy Strings, plus a wider bill including Caroline Polachek, Underscores, Remi Wolf, Westside Cowboy, Horsegiirl, Tiffany Day, and more. Check out the full slate below. Hinterland 2027 takes place from July 30 to August 1.

Since its first edition in 2015, Hinterland has been held in St. Charles, which sits a roughly 30-minute drive south of Des Moines. The 2026 lineup boasted Oklou, Ninajirachi, Lorde, Jane Remover, Geese, and Kali Uchis, among others.

All three of Hinterland’s headliners next year will be performing on the heels of hot-ticket tours. Bridgers wraps up the European leg of her dates in support of Lost Weekend this December, and Billy Strings just extended a 2027 run behind the T Bone Burnett-produced So Much for Goodbyes through next June. Slayyyter, who concluded her Wor$t Girl in the World trek last month, will precede her Hinterland show with a Madison Square Garden headlining debut.

entry.title: Oklou Scored a New Animated Film
entry.summary: The first song off the In Waves soundtrack, “The Swirl Ahead," is out now
entry.content:
Oklou has penned the score for a new animated feature, In Waves, set to land on Netflix next month. She collaborated with the French artist ROB on the 23-song soundtrack, which is out alongside the film on December 11. You can check out a first preview, “The Swirl Ahead,” below.

Directed by Phuong Mai Nguyen, In Waves is adapted from AJ Dungo’s 2019 graphic memoir of the same name, which charts the romance between a young surfer and skateboarder as they pursue their passions and navigate personal struggles. It premiered earlier this year at Cannes Film Festival, becoming the first animated film selected to open Cannes’ Critics Week.

The release caps off a big year for Oklou, who just closed out the second run of an extensive tour in support of her 2025 album Choke Enough. The trek included her Coachella debut back in April, plus headlining dates at Primavera Sound, Lollapalooza, and All Points East. Last year, she also released a deluxe edition of the album that featured a song with FKA twigs, “Viscus.”

Revisit Anna Gaca’s 2025 cover story Oklou’s Endless Summer.
